Across all, hollow rectangular outlines moved to the top of the same grid, and non-enclosing forms moved to the bottom, retaining their original columns and shapes. Demo3 also shows same-color 8 outline and open cross in same columns can end at opposite edges: frame top, cross bottom. Test task input 16x15 contained: color3 3x3 hollow frame at rows2-4 cols3-5; color8 open 4x3 motif rows3-6 cols0-2; color2 open 4x5 motif rows1-4 cols10-14; color1 hollow 3x4 frame rows6-8 cols4-7; color1 hollow 5x5 frame rows6-10 cols10-14; color2 plus rows10-12 cols0-2. Several outputs based on hypothesized class-directed edge movement, with variations in stacking order and handling cross-class obstruction, all failed. Therefore do NOT assume simple hollow-up/open-down packing is sufficient for this task; unresolved mechanism likely involves interaction/collision, alignment, or a different object rule. 8 guesses were wrong. Keep this as negative/uncertain evidence, not a solution.', global_=True)
